about: Pool-method comparison for the thin T20I pools, produced by `node sensitivity.mjs --pool-methods`. Primary = own-pool (the method used for the submitted lists). Alternatives = format-fallback (C1), shrunk (C2), adjacent-fallback (C3). The criterion in `preregistered` was fixed before any candidate was run (pool_preregistration.md). No timestamps.

rules.1: M1 candidate <= 0.85 x M1 BASE in all four cells (S1, S2 x batters, bowlers)
rules.2: S2 batters: mean(M2a, M2b) rises by >= 0.02, or mean(M3a, M3b) falls by >= 10% relative
rules.3: no harm in all four cells: M2a, M2b >= BASE - 0.01; M3a, M3b <= BASE + 0.5; M4 <= BASE + 0.005; M5-all >= BASE - 0.02
rules.4: eligible counts (batters, bowlers, all-rounders) identical to BASE, S1 and S2
rules.5: large-pool players (no profile in a thin stratum): max |index change| <= 1.0 and max |rank change| <= 5, S1 and S2
rules.6: players with a profile in a thin stratum: max |index change| <= 5.0, S1 and S2
rules.7: S1: at most 3 top-10 names change per list (batters, bowlers, all-rounders)

preregistered.decision: Candidates failing any rule are rejected. One passer: adopt. Several: larger mean relative M1 reduction over the four cells; within 2 percentage points: fewer S1 indexes changed, then simpler (C1, C3, C2). None: KEEP_CURRENT.

methods.label: current method: each stratum standardised against its own pool
a stratum with 10 or fewer eligible profiles uses all seasons of the same format
every stratum: mean and variance shrunk toward all seasons of the format, pseudo-count 5
